description.narrative:
Non-Governmental Gender Organisations Coordinating Council (NGOCC) i Zambia har ansökt om stöd till ett värde av 40 miljoner SEK för att implementera sin strategiska plan för perioden 2018 till 2022.
Insatsens syfte är att öka kvinnors och flickors tillgång till och kontroll över resurser, sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa, representation och politiskt deltagande på alla nivåer, och minska kvinnors utsatthet för klimatförändringar. NGOCC kommer att implementera insatsen genom sina medlemsorganisationer.
Insatsens totala budget uppgår till 97 miljoner SEK (ZMW 109 miljoner). Utav den totala budgeten så utgörs cirka 4,4 miljoner SEK av organisationens egna medel och 17,8 miljoner av medel från andra givare (WeEffect, IM Sverige, EU, CHAZ och NED). De återstående 74,8 miljonerna (SEK) är inte säkrade ännu. Cirka 23,3 miljoner SEK av den totala budgeten kommer att vidareförmedlas från NGOCC genom organisationens Basket Fund.

The Non-Governmental Gender Organisations Coordinating Council (NGOCC) in Zambia has applied to Sida for funding of 40 million SEK to implement their strategic plan "Building Solidarity for Women's Empowerment" for the period 2018 to 2022.
The intervention aims at improving women's and girls' access to and control of resources, sexual and reproductive health, representation and participation of women in governance and leadership at all levels and reducing vulnerability of women to climate change impacts and strengthening their capacity to manage natural resources. NGOCC will implement the intervention with its member organisations.
The intervention’s total budget is 97 million SEK (ZMW 109million), out of which the organisation’s own funding is approximately 4.4 million SEK (ZMW 4.9 million), other donor funding from We Effect, IM Swedish, the EU, CHAZ & NED is 17.8 million SEK (ZMW 20 million) and the remaining 74.8 million SEK (ZMW 83.9 million) not yet secured. Approximately 23.3 million SEK (ZMW 26 million) of the intervention budget will be forwarded from NGOCC to sub-grantees through its 'Basket Fund' .
To contribute to women's empowerment and gender equality in Zambia.

description.narrative:
Objective 1: Improved cultural norms, practices and beliefs towards gender equity and equality
- Traditional leaders were engaged on combating harmful traditional practices such as child marriage. As a result of this engagement, 36 traditional leaders including chiefs and village heads resolved and committed to end child marriage in their chiefdoms by ensuring that By-Laws were in place and publicised.
Objective 2: Improved policy/legal frameworks for women and girl's empowerment
- NGOCC engaged with the Republican Vice President, government ministries and agencies as well as parliament on a range of issues including the re-establishment of the Gender Ministry, the operationalisation of the Gender Equity and Equality Act (GEEA), gender responsive budgeting and planning, and access to the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) for women. The outcomes of these engagements are yet to be seen.
- NGOCC has been using the Household Approach as a gender transformative approach to inclusive decision making at household level. The feedback from women in some of the communities suggest that some good results have been achieved as reflected in the quotes below:
Alina Mabuto (53-year-old) Kabwe resident is one of the beneficiaries of the household approach training under Kafwa Organisation for Female Prisoners and had this to say;
Before the training I had challenges with decision making and budgets in my home due to lack of knowledge, as all the decisions were being made by my husband as he was the head of the house. After I was trained and have now started engaging my husband on issues that need us to make decisions and budgeting in our home. With the support from my husband and children I have now started rearing village chickens as an income generating and this has now started contributing towards my familys basic needs because we are now economically stable as a household".
Elina Chilala had this to say;
I am very happy to have been sensitised together with my husband on making joint decisions in our home. My husband used to make decisions on his own and we just used to follow and do what he tells me to do. But after the Moono Area Association taught us on how to budget and work together for the best result. I have seen it with my own eyes, my husband since we got married, he called me, and we budgeted together before taking the maize to FRA and when we sold the produce the money that we were given we followed the budget and also paid school fees for our children who are at college.
Objective 3: Improved resilience through women and girl's empowerment
- Women in some of the NGOCC operational areas have adopted the use of clean energy products including solar lamps. This has enhanced the quality of life and also improved women's small businesses. Some quotes below refer:
"The solar lighting has really changed our lives because we are no longer dependent on traditional lamps lighting which was hazardous and houses were prone to catch fire but now we sleep peacefully without any worries that our children after studying will doze off and leave the traditional lamp or candle on said one of the women from Mutaba Womens Area Association"
Speaking on cook stoves, one beneficiary had this to say;
"We are thankful for this project that you have brought here in Judah and Sokoni villages of Kapiri Mposhi because you have eased our chores with these energy efficient cook stoves which you have introduced in our villages. We dont have to walk long distances to fetch firewood but instead we only need twigs said the women of Kapiri Mposhi district".
- It was reported that 77 women out of the 311 who attended climate change awareness meetings adopted smart farming methods including intercropping. The community members reported growing a variety of crops, namely: maize, sunflower, cotton, soya beans and monkey peas.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
